finding.claim: The named-pipe client connects to whatever server owns the predictable pipe name without verifying the server's PID, owner, or integrity level, so a local process can squat the pipe name and receive the victim's agent requests (public keys and signing challenges) and return forged responses.
finding.source: Predictable pipe name built from the OS username (namedpipes.rs:49-53, 55-93) and a public, unkeyed hash suffix (namedpipes.rs:95-121). Attacker needs a local process able to create a named pipe in \\.\pipe\ with the victim's username, while the victim's Pageant is not serving.
finding.sink: ClientOptions::new().open(&pipe_name) at namedpipes.rs:33; agent requests are then written to the attacker-controlled server via the AsyncWrite delegate (namedpipes.rs:137-161).

trace.note: PageantStream::new tries namedpipes first on Windows
namedpipes::PageantStream::new called; success returns NamedPipes variant without further checks
username from get_username (OS account, not secret)
suffix from capi_obfuscate_string, a deterministic SHA-256 over CryptProtectMemory output with CROSS_PROCESS and no secret
ClientOptions::open connects to the pipe server with no server-identity check
only ERROR_PIPE_BUSY is retried; any other failure returns error, so fallback only happens when open fails

finding.guards_checked: Username is OS-derived and not attacker-controlled (no injection into the pipe path). No server-identity verification (GetNamedPipeServerProcessId, owner or token check) exists anywhere on the path. ERROR_PIPE_BUSY retry loop (namedpipes.rs:31-44) only handles busy pipes, not impersonation. Pipe fallback in lib.rs:22-58 is not reached when a squatter's pipe opens successfully. Default pipe DACL that would decide whether another local account can create the pipe was NOT verified (UNCERTAIN). Impact is limited: no private key material exposed and signatures cannot be forged, but public keys, signing challenges, and auth availability are affected.
